heroSubtitle: Intelligent Threat Detection System for Haramaya University
heroDescription: Harness the power of artificial intelligence to monitor, detect, and respond to cyber threats across Haramaya University's digital infrastructure. Sentinel AI provides real-time threat intelligence, automated alerts, and actionable insights to protect academic and administrative systems.
howItWorksSubtitle: From raw logs to actionable insights
step1Desc: Collect data from firewalls, servers, and network devices across campus.
step2Desc: Models analyze patterns and detect anomalies using supervised & unsupervised techniques.
step3Desc: Identify DDoS, malware, brute-force, and unauthorized access attempts.
step4Desc: Real-time alerts with severity, location, and recommended actions.
aboutSubtitle: Intelligent threat detection for Haramaya University
aboutPara1: Sentinel AI is an advanced cybersecurity system that leverages machine learning to monitor, detect, and respond to cyber threats across Haramaya University's network infrastructure. The system continuously analyzes network traffic, authentication logs, and system events to identify anomalies and potential attacks in real time.
aboutPara2: Key capabilities include AI-powered threat detection, area-based visualization of attacks across campus zones, intelligent alert prioritization with confidence scoring, and automated security reporting. Sentinel AI provides security administrators with a unified dashboard for complete situational awareness and rapid incident response.

campusZoneMappingDescription: Campus zone mapping and traffic context - used as input for AI threat detection, not network control.
contextualDataNote: This contextual data is derived from aggregated network logs (source IP, protocol, packet size, etc.) and is used by the Area Map and Analytics modules to visualize threat distribution across campus zones. No packet filtering, firewall rules, or traffic shaping is performed here.
problemDescription: Haramaya University relies on interconnected platforms such as student portals, learning management systems, financial systems, and campus networks. Traditional security measures—firewalls, manual log reviews, and signature-based antivirus—cannot detect sophisticated, slow-moving, or previously unseen attacks. As a result, the university remains vulnerable to:
problemDelayedIncidentResponse: Delayed incident response and lack of centralized monitoring
problemRiskToSensitiveData: Risk to sensitive academic, research, and administrative data
solutionDescription: Sentinel AI replaces reactive, rule-based security with AI-driven, real-time threat detection. The system:
solutionCollectsPreprocesses: Collects and preprocesses network logs, authentication records, and system events
solutionUsesMachineLearning: Uses machine learning (Random Forest, SVM, and deep learning models) to classify threats and assign severity levels with confidence scores
solutionProvidesDashboard: Provides a centralized dashboard for live visualization of attacks, campus-area-based threat maps, and historical trends
solutionSendsAlerts: Sends automated alerts and generates periodic reports for administrators
realTimeMonitoringDescription: Continuous analysis of network devices, servers, and endpoints
anomalyThreatDetectionDescription: ML-based classification of malicious activities (e.g., brute force, DDoS, insider threats)
interactiveDashboardDescription: Dashboard with heatmaps, severity indicators, and live alert feeds
automatedReportingDescription: On-demand and scheduled reports with threat summaries and actionable insights
roleBasedAccessDescription: Secure access for system administrators and security analysts
teamDescription: Sentinel AI was designed and developed as a final year project by four Computer Science students at Haramaya University, College of Computing and Informatics (CCI).
intendedUsersDescription: IT administrators and security analysts at Haramaya University
scopeDescription: Real-time monitoring, detection, alerting, and reporting – not automatic prevention (human-in-the-loop)
environmentDescription: Designed to operate within the university's existing network and server infrastructure
detectionAccuracyDescription: High precision on known attack patterns; some false positives may occur due to unusual but benign student activity (e.g., late-night research)
encryptedTrafficDescription: Analysis is limited to packet metadata (size, timing) when content is encrypted (HTTPS/VPN)
latencyDescription: Real-time processing is subject to campus network load and available hardware resources
areaMappingAccuracyDescription: IP-to-building mapping depends on the university's IP registration data
